speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) in respect of the percentage of Polytechnic and ITE graduates securing permanent, full-time employment within a year of their graduation (a) what has been the statistical trend over the past 10 years; and (b) what are the reasons behind the trend.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Having said that, there have been some significant shifts in the choices of graduates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: This is driven by various efforts of the Government to expand education pathways for students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: There are more places at polytechnics for ITE students, and more places at universities for polytechnic students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: As for those who choose to enter the labour force, there has also been a shift.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Full-time permanent work has come down, while freelance, part-time and temporary work have gone up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: A similar proportion chose not to do full-time permanent work voluntarily.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: They could be doing freelance work or have other reasons to lead them to choose to work part-time or take up temporary employment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: The strong desire to further their studies, higher incidence of students choosing to do freelance work or start their own business and students taking longer to look for work, are possible explanations for these changes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Some economists have opined that technical jobs may be more at risk from trends, such as automation, robotics, artificial intelligence.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does the Ministry feel that the outlook for these jobs is more at risk going forward because of these developments as compared to other kinds of jobs, for example, graduate jobs?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we will continue to study the matter to ensure that there are factors that we can address to benefit the students as best we can.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is early days in terms of the shifts with respect to the behaviour I described in the first part of my answer, so we will continue to study it.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But so far, the Earn and Learn Programme appears to be doing well.
